title: TEG CHAND versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010161302026
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Criminal No. 1857 of 2026
 Before the National Lok Adalat
Teg Chand and Another --Petitioners
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Chandramauli Shah, learned counsel for the petitioners,
Mrs. Minakshi Sharma, learned AGA with Mr. Virendra Rawat,
learned AGA for the State.
Mr. Amit Kapri, learned counsel for the respondent nos.3 & 4.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
By means of this criminal writ petition filed
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the
petitioners have sought the following reliefs:-
"(1) Issue an order, direction or writ in the nature
of certiorari quashing of First Information Report
dated 25.03.2024 lodged by the respondent no.3
as F.I.R. No. 0015/2024, under Section- 323 of
The Indian Penal Code & 3(1)(x) of The Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act, P.S. Dharchula, District
Pithoragarh, against the petitioner's (Annexure
No.2 to the writ petition Page No.l6 to 21.).
(ii) Issue an order, direction or writ in the nature
of mandamus directing Respondent No.1& 2 not to
arrest the petitioner in First Information Report
dated 25.03.2024 lodged by the respondent no.3
as F.I.R. No. 0015/2024, under Section-323 of
The Indian Penal Code & 3(1)(x) of The Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act, P.S. Dharchula, District
Pithoragarh, against the petitioner's (Annexure
1

No.2 to the writ petition Page No.16 to 21).
(iii) Issue any other appropriate order or direction
as the Hon'ble Court thinks fit and proper.
(iv) To award the cost to the petitioner."
2. Mr. Chandramauli Shah, learned counsel for
the petitioners-accused.
3. Mrs. Minakshi Sharma, learned AGA with Mr.
V.S. Rawat, learned AGA for the State.
4. Mr. Amit Kapri, learned counsel for the
respondent nos.3 & 4.
5. The petitioners and respondent nos.3 & 4 are
present through video conferencing and they are duly
identified by their respective counsel.
6. Both, the petitioners and respondent nos.3 &
4 submitted that they have filed a Compounding
Application (IA No.1 of 2026) and affidavits with their
free will and without any pressure. Today, they have
filed a Compromise Memo.
7. On interaction, respondent no.3-Naresh
Singh states that the matter has been settled between
the parties and he does not want to prosecute the
petitioners any further. Similar statements have been
made in the affidavits filed in support of the
compounding application.
2

UKHC010161302026
8. Both the parties submitted that they have
resolved their private disputes amicably. They have
filed a Compromise Memo.
9. Learned counsel for the State submitted that
although offenses under the SC/ST Act are non-compoundable, there are private disputes between the
parties and they have resolved their disputes,
therefore, the State has no objection to the
Compounding Application (IA No.1 of 2026).
10. In the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court
in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, 2012
(10) SCC 303, Dimpey Gujral vs. Union Territory,
Chandigarh, (2013) 11 SCC 497, B.S. Joshi vs. State of
Haryana, (2003) 4 SCC 675 and Nikhil Merchant vs.
CBI, (2008) 9 SCC 677, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has
permitted compounding of non-compoundable offences.
11. In the present case, the parties have entered
into a compromise and the dispute is personal in
nature, putting the matter through trial would be a
futile exercise.
12. Keeping in view the totality of the facts and
circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that
ends of justice would be met if the compounding
application is allowed and the First Information Report
3

UKHC010161302026
dated 25.03.2024, lodged by the respondent no.3 as
FIR No.0015/2024 under Section 323 IPC and Section
3(1)(x) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, are quashed.
Compounding application is accordingly allowed.
13. Resultantly, the First Information Report
dated 25.03.2024, lodged by the respondent no.3 as
FIR No.0015/2024, P.S. Dharchula, District Pithoragarh
under Section 323 IPC and Section 3(1)(x) of the
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act, are hereby quashed.
14. The Criminal Writ Petition No.1857 of 2026 is
disposed of accordingly.
15. The Compounding Application and the
Compromise Memo shall form part of this order.
